topic: Unit 5: A2 Themes (Young People in Society; Our Place in a Changing World)
subject: french

items.title: Where most French speakers will live
items.claim: OIF (Observatoire de la langue francaise) projections suggest that by 2050, roughly what share of French speakers will live in Africa?
items.reveal_title: Most French speakers will be African
items.reveal:
OIF estimates (Demographie et langue francaise reports) project that demographic growth in francophone Africa will lift the African share of French speakers to around 85% by 2050.

This follows from population growth in countries such as DR Congo, where French is an official or working language.
items.why: The geographic centre of a language can shift dramatically across a generation.

items.title: Subjunctive use today
items.claim: The imparfait du subjonctif is widely described as moribund in modern French. In what context might it still appear?

options.text: In very formal literary writing, often for stylistic effect

items.reveal:
The form survives in writing for archaic or formal register. Spoken French typically uses the present subjunctive where the imperfect would be classical.

Grevisse's Le Bon Usage remains a standard reference describing the changing patterns.
items.why: Grammatical change is often gradual, leaving an archaic register that signals formality.

items.title: When the Academie was founded
items.claim: The Academie francaise was established to regulate the French language. In which year and under whose authority?
items.reveal:
Richelieu gave letters patent on 29 January 1635. The Academie has 40 'immortels' and has been working on its Dictionnaire since 1694 (first edition).

The ninth edition has been in progress since 1986 and was completed in 2024.
items.why: Language regulation in France is a centuries-long state project, not a recent reaction to globalisation.
